summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of atrial fibrillation, hypertension, diabetes, and heart failure was admitted after experiencing acute left arm weakness and coordination difficulties upon waking. Initial evaluation revealed a subtherapeutic INR of 1.2 due to poor anticoagulation adherence. Imaging showed no hemorrhage on CT, but MRI confirmed an acute embolic stroke in the right parietal lobe, with additional small infarcts in the cerebellum and temporal regions. The patient was managed with IV heparin and increased warfarin dosing, eventually reaching an INR of 1.9 at discharge. He experienced mild orthopnea during admission, but cardiac evaluation showed stable heart function with no acute changes. He improved neurologically and was discharged home with medication adjustments, including increased statin and continued anticoagulation, along with close follow-up for INR monitoring and cardiology care.
